title: What is known about 1RB0RB_0LC0RA_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RB_0LC0RA_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is a counter at the left end followed by a long alternating stretch (10)^n holding a single marker 0. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps; an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells) finds no halt in the first 1015 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 4,657 cells have been visited and 2,326 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.345). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.298).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells) runs 1015 steps without a halt. The macro simulator cuts the tape into blocks of K cells, run-length codes them, and crosses a whole run at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with; it agrees with the plain simulator tools/c/tmrun cell for cell.

claims.title: A marker counted in base 3
claims.text: At the moments the head first reaches a new cell on the left, the tape ends in (10)^x 0 (10)^y; between consecutive such moments x fell by 243 (79 times), 81 (70), 27 (34), 9 (8), 729 (6) and a handful of other amounts in the first 108 steps, and rose 143 times (resets).

claims.title: The halting state, seen from the run
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps state D was entered 74,578 times, always reading a 0 (D1 halts).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. A marker 0 drifts left through a long alternating sea while a counter at the left end, written in pieces 1110, counts the sweeps; when the marker reaches the far end the sea is reset, a little longer.

facts.text: No halt in an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells).
The marker moves 27, 81, 243, 729 cells between left growths: a sweep counter.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the C simulator; 4,657 cells visited.

sections.heading: What the machine does
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell. With a for 10, around step 9.5·107:

The right part is an alternating sea a^x 0 a^y with one extra 0, the marker, and x + y fixed within a round (791 + 243 and 62 + 972 in the round that starts at step 94,966,670). The marker moves left. The left part is made of pieces 1^2 a^k with small k and changes like a counter: the tape grows on the left only when the counter gains a piece, and between left growths the marker moved by powers of 3. In the first 108 steps the decrements of x between left growths were 243 (79 times), 81 (70), 27 (34), 9 (8), 729 (6) and a handful of others, and x was reset upward 143 times.

This is the sweep counter of 1RB0RE_1LC1RD_1LD0LD_0RE0LC_1RA1RF_0RA--- and 1RB1RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RE_1LE0LE_0RA0LD_0RB---, mirrored: here the counter sits at the left end and the marker moves left. A round of a sea of width w is about w sweeps of about w steps, so the width grows like the cube root of the step count.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The halting transition is D reading a 1. D is entered only from C reading a 1 (1LD), so a halt needs 1 C>1. In the first 108 steps D was entered 74,578 times, every time on a 0, and 74,124 of those times at least 7 cells from the right end.
Whether the counter's carries or the resets can ever put C on a 1 with a 1 to its left is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.345). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.298).
After 109 steps the tape spans 4,657 cells (3,548 left of the start, 252 right), with a density of 1s of 0.499.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: sweep counter: a marker in an alternating sea, counted in base 3
summary: A marker 0 drifts left through a long alternating sea while a counter at the left end, written in pieces 1110, counts the sweeps; when the marker reaches the far end the sea is reset, a little longer.
